title: Mounting
note: Items that mount on a building (a breaker box, a light, a solar panel on a roof or ground mount). See docs/ATTACHED_ITEMS.md.

attach_surface.label: Mounts On
attach_surface.note: chimney = a chimney kit: aimed at an OUTSIDE wall of a finished building from outside or from inside, it builds a brick or stone chimney (stack outside, mantel and firebox inside, a metre past the roof; Growth/Chimney.cs, docs/CHIMNEYS.md). Otherwise: an item that mounts on a FINISHED building instead of standing on the ground: wall (a breaker box, a wall sconce, a switch), ceiling (a ceiling light) or roof (a solar rack: aimed at the roof from the GROUND, there are no ladders; it lies on the roof surface with its long side up the slope). With the item in hand a left click brings out a preview over the walls / ceiling, a second click or Enter mounts it, a right click takes it down. Leave empty for everything else. Such an item is not placeable (placeable false). See docs/ATTACHED_ITEMS.md. Model: the back of a wall item is the plane y = 0 sticking out towards -y; a ceiling item hangs from its top.

attach_side.label: Mount Side
attach_side.note: For a wall mount: which side of the wall it goes on. interior = inside a room (switches, sconces), exterior = outside the building (a breaker box, a wall lantern), either = both.

attach_through.label: Through The Wall
attach_through.note: A wall item (attach_surface wall, either side) that goes THROUGH the wall, like a wire entry: its model has a node 'Plate' (the face plate on the aimed side, its back on the plane y = 0 and its front towards -y in Blender) and a node 'Pipe' (a sleeve 0.25 m long going into the wall, towards +y in Blender). The game measures the wall, lengthens the pipe to it and puts a second plate on the other side, so the item shows and is clicked from both sides. See docs/ATTACHED_ITEMS.md.

attach_item.label: Mount Takes Item
attach_item.note: A mount (a solar rack) takes this item (a solar panel): a right click on the placed mount with the item in hand fits it. Item id; pairs with attach_result. The item itself should not be placeable (placeable false): it only goes on its mount.

attach_result.label: Mount Becomes
attach_result.note: What the mount becomes once its attach_item is fitted (the rack with its panel, a separate item with its own model). It is not for sale; a roof one has attach_surface roof like the mount.

wrench_remove.label: Bolted Down (Wrench)
wrench_remove.note: A placed item that is bolted down: a right click picks it up only with a wrench (adjustable or pipe) in the active slot; without one it says to use a wrench. The kitchen, living room, lighting and bathroom packs set it.

roof_mount.label: Also Mounts On A Roof
roof_mount.note: A placeable item that may ALSO be put up on a finished building's roof (a dish, a yagi, an access point): aimed at the roof from the ground it stands upright there, and R turns it 22.5 degrees a press (also once it is up, with the cursor on it). A wrench (Shift + right click) takes it down.

provides_power.label: Brings Power
provides_power.note: Mounted on the OUTSIDE of a building it brings electricity to that building (the outdoor breaker box). Lights whose manifest entry says requires_power stay dark in a building without it.

panel_offset_m.label: Panel Height (m)
panel_offset_m.note: A solar mount: how far above the mount's origin the fitted panel's underside sits (a roof mount 0.10, a ground rack the height of its low edge plus half the slope).

panel_width_m.label: Panel Width (m)
panel_width_m.note: A solar mount: the width of the panel it takes seen from above. Mounts snap to each other this far apart so the panels do not overlap.

panel_depth_m.label: Panel Depth (m)
panel_depth_m.note: A solar mount: the depth of its panel seen from above (a tilted panel is shorter from above than it is long).

panel_tilt_deg.label: Panel Tilt (deg)
panel_tilt_deg.note: A solar mount: the fitted panel's tilt about the X axis (0 flat on a roof, 30 on a ground rack).
